text.p: MicroEnergy Inc said Tuesday it expects to report a substantial operating loss for the fourth quarter ending June 30.
The company said the loss was due primarily to the delay of its public offering, which was completed in July, which caused customers to defer placement of orders.
MicroEnergy also said it expects to report revenues of $14.4 million for fiscal 1995, compared with $14.6 million a year ago.
MicroEnergy said it expects to benefit from delayed orders beginning in early fiscal 1997, and sees 25 to 30 percent revenue growth in fiscal 1997 compared with $14.4 million in fiscal 1996.
The company added it expects to return to operating profitability for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1997.

"The actions we are already taking are expected to enable MicroEnergy to achieve profitability in 1997 and aggressively develop our long-term strategies to market a broader line of products across an expanding market," Robert Gatza, chief executive officer, said in a statement. "We do not view the (fourth quarter) operating loss as the beginning of a negative trend in quarterly results."

He added that the additional capital raised from the recent public offering was nearly $2.8 million. "This now enables us to fund the anticipated increase in business, improve operating efficiencies, and to respond more effiectively to changing market trends," he said.
MicroEnergy makes high frequency power supplies and converters.
